You know who I'm talking about, that guy who does all sorts of stupid shit, but never quite enough to get kicked out of military, and if it weren't so damn funny, the command would have made up a reason to kick him out. You know, like littering in front of battalion, and then trying to out run the former Special Forces/Delta Battalion Commander because he's in civilian attire and he didn't recognize him, and even though his hair is graying he has like a 3000 AFPT score.

I know that guy, because that was me.

I have hundreds of stories, and the stitches to prove them, but this incident is the one that put PV2 Peen on the map. Everyone in the battalion knew who I was after this one.

I was a Bradley driver for most of my first two years in the Army. If you don't know what a Bradley is, look it up, it's a multimillion dollar piece of shit that has no place on the battlefield. It's constantly broken, and is an ecological disaster how much that thing leaks.

It was mid-spring if I remember correctly, because there was no snow on the ground, the grass was green, and it wasn't hot out, probably sweater weather. I had been in the Army for less than a year. We were out in the field doing some light Bradley training, platoon engagements and whatnot with the MILES gear before the live fire stuff. It was only like a two week field problem, so we weren't at a training site with dedicated OpFor, just guys picked from another battalion in our brigade.

I forget exactly what the mission was, but we were cresting a hilltop looking for the OpFor village.

"Ok, gunner, scan right."

I spot the "village" to our left. It's just a few plywood buildings, so I call it out, "Sergeant, the village is to the left."

"Shut the fuck up, Peen, this training is for the gunner."

My vehicle commander was a bit of a hothead. A real dick. Knew his shit, was a good trainer, but many many many of times he would just loose his shit, start throwing tools at people, yell a bunch, and stomp off. We were a really bad match for a crew because I would start laughing when he would go into a rage fit, and that would only make him more engaged.

"Roger, Sergeant, I'm just saying the village is over there to the left, I can see it from..."

"SHUT THE FUCK UP PEEN! Ok, gunner, scan left."

Now the turret is facing almost right at the village, but for some reason neither the gunner nor the vehicle commander can see it. "Ok, scan back right."

I don't know why I didn't have my headset set on Push To Talk, but this situation probably wouldn't have escalated if I didn't have an open mic. "Y'all were just on it. It's to the left."

"SHUT THE FUCK UP PEEN!!! I WILL PULL YOU OUT OF THAT HATCH AND STOMP YOUR FUCKING SKULL IN! SHUT THE FUCK UP! GUNNER, SCAN BACK LEFT."

Our gunner is finally like, "Ok, I see it now, there it is."

Open mic again, "Told you so.", oh, and this wasn't like a quick "told you so", more like a "tooold you sooo"

I can't ALL-CAPS or bold enough to convey the amount of rage spewing from the vehicle commander at this point, but the last part of it was "Shut the fuck up, Peen, and fucking floor it!"

I turn the track towards the village, and floor it. The Bradley only goes about 40 mph on a flat surface, but we're heading a good angle down hill, and this beast weighs about 28 tons not combat loaded, and we have dismounts in the back. I want to say that we're probably going about 45-50 mph downhill when I spot a ditch at the bottom of the hill, so I ease up on the gas.

"WHY THE FUCK ARE WE SLOWING DOWN?! I SAID FUCKING FLOOR IT!!!"

"But Serge..."

"I SAID SHUT THE FUCK UP AND FLOOR IT!!"

"Sergeant, there's a...!"

Rage mode x10, "FUCKING FLOOR IT!! SHUT THE FUCK UP AND FLOOR IT!!!"

So I shut the fuck up and pressed the pedal to the metal....

Right before we hit the ditch I hear over my headset, "oh fuck.."

Upon impact my helmet hits the top of the driver's hatch, slides forward until my shoulder blades hit the top of the hatch. Everything is in slow motion, it feels like zero G. I bounce back into the seat in time to see through the driver periscope grass rushing in front of it... The vehicle is pointed nose down, still moving.

The second impact is much much more violent. I swear my tailbone hit the top of the driver's hatch. The vehicle is no longer moving, the engine is no longer running, the engine access panel is flipped open, there's smoke and dust rising, blood dripping from my mouth, and the smell of JP8 everywhere. The dismounts yell to drop the ramp, so I do.

I'm just sitting there in the driver's hole, heart racing, still in shock, expecting the vehicle commander to flip open my hatch, pull me out, and murder me... but he doesn't come. That's when I start to worry. I see OpFor running out of the woods to our position.

I climb out, go to the top of the vehicle, and look down his hatch, but he's not in there. My gunner is climbing out, and he's pissed off, but I don't see the vehicle commander. I go around to the back of the vehicle, and all the dismounts are on the ground moaning. The vehicle commander is sitting there in the back, "You did that on purpose..."

I don't say anything....

OpFor gets there, the medics pull up. One of the OpFor says that he's never seen anything like it before, the Bradley flew.

The medics took everyone complaining away, about 6, but I think 4 of them were just faking, trying to get out of the field problem. My gunner isn't pissed that I did it, he's just like, "I know you did that shit on purpose.. You just gotta warn me before you do something like that."

I denied it all around.

While the mechanics were working on the vehicle, a buddy and I went and followed the track marks from the hill to where the vehicle landed. You could see the tracks coming down the hill, to the ditch, and then they disappeared at the top of the ditch. There was a road along the the ditch, no track marks, and then about 5 feet after the road, track marks start again and the vehicle. It flew for about 15 feet vertical distance.

4 of the guys who went to the aid station were sent right back out. My vehicle commander needed 6 stitches in his knee. One guy got held for a day because of possible concussion, but he was back training the next day. The vehicle had a busted fuel line, but the mechanics had it up and running in an hour or two.

I denied the fuck out of that. I said that I saw the ditch, but I didn't think it was that deep or that I thought the vehicle commander had a better view than I did.

Around the battalion everyone knew me as the guy who got a Bradley airborne. They joked about getting me an airborne badge, and my buddies would always say that line from Back to the Future, "Roads, where we're going we don't need roads."

As for if I did that on purpose? Wrecked a multimillion dollar military vehicle and sent 6 people to the aid station just to get back at my vehicle commander being a royal dick?

Nah, I didn't think the ditch was that deep, and I thought the vehicle commander had a better view from up top ;)

But seriously, that's the truth.
